## Overview

Fixes #49250 and addresses the stale-placeholder/request-stall mechanism in #45138. When a synchronous external KV load fails under `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, restore accepted request state in the scheduler and Model Runner V2 before decoding resumes.

## Claims

- Retire discarded in-flight output without changing the recovered request state.
- Restore V2 token history, sequence length, penalty counts, speculative state, and Mamba alignment state from the scheduler's accepted position.
- Order repair of shared KV blocks, prevent new prefix-cache hits on invalid blocks, and transfer unfinished repair ownership when an owner leaves after failure handling.

## Validation

At current head `1eca68f4`:

- [Author CPU validation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-6187605605): 497 selected cases passed. The after-report abort/preempt reproducer's two recompute cases fail on base; all four cases pass here.
- [Independent CPU validation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-6196459351): 74 recovery and invalid-block cases passed.
- [Targeted GPU validation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-6160858646): the suffix-rewind test passed, including non-negative penalty counts. Full-model GPU checks below belong to earlier revisions.

The upstream executor/connector CI lanes still require maintainer authorization, requested in the author validation comment above.

The historical local `22fdd4d9be` threshold-64 GPU dual-oracle result was **3/4**, with an unaffected request differing at a BF16 tie. This is not an all-output equality claim.

<details>
<summary>GPU history, reproduction and validation limits</summary>

Rejected requests are compared against connector-free recomputation; unaffected requests are compared against successful reuse. State and shared-block ordering are checked separately from exact token equality.

- [Independent GB200 run](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-6132316001), `c261cdee` applied to `main` `fabaecbf`: Qwen3-0.6B recovers where base asserts; the rejected prompt matches recomputation and the three unaffected prompts retain reuse output. 156 tests passed.
- [Independent GH200 run](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-5442764086), `f2e2abd460`: both rejected requests match recomputation and both unaffected requests match reuse.
- Local RTX 5060 Ti run, `22fdd4d9be` on base `eed1f3d0c6`: 330 tests passed and ten cold GPU cells completed. OPT-125M matched all eight baseline tokens after a rejected 16-token load with zero copied bytes. Qwen ordering passed at threshold 32 in sync/async modes and threshold 64 in sync mode. Threshold-64 exact dual-oracle equality was 3/4; threshold-32 whole-output differences also remained.
- Earlier controlled rejection covered sync, async, and async EAGLE3; real `LMCacheConnectorV1` negative controls covered sync and async. Failure was injected before KV copying. Direct old-versus-patched GPU controls also verified sampled-token/count rollback and Mamba offsets 0, 8, and 9.

The earlier local eight-file regression command was:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_kv_connector.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py
```

The 497-case CPU selection linked above is a separate run. Applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed in the earlier rebase validation. Updating this description did not rerun tests.

Not validated: real multi-GPU/NCCL execution, full-model Mamba/RecoverSSM load rejection, layerwise loading, partial-copy failure, performance, or cross-hardware bitwise determinism.

</details>

## Details

Scheduler rollback alone leaves device state from discarded frames. An explicit `rewound_req_ids` signal restores V2 state, while scheduler barriers prevent dependent requests from reading shared blocks before repair is safe. These parts address the same recovery sequence; there is no connector-specific special case.

<details>
<summary>Related work, remaining timing gaps and acknowledgements</summary>

#49252 derives a frame count from placeholders and excludes speculative decoding. This PR uses exact in-flight token accounting and an explicit worker rewind. #59793 covers the scheduler portion; [its author reviewed this PR and prefers it to land](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-6157413424), keeping #59793 as a fallback.

**Before-report gaps remain separate.** Aborting before the failure report can leave invalid blocks reusable, tracked in #61768 and addressed by #61769. Overlaying #61769 at `7238ccdf` onto `1eca68f4` passed 519 author CPU cases and 96 independent CPU cases. Those totals include the overlay and are not results for this PR alone. The [latest independent check](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-6196459351) also reports preemption before the failure report, which neither PR covers. If #61769 lands first, this PR will need a rebase retaining both sets of helper assertions.

Acknowledgements:

- @ayoub-ibm reported and diagnosed #49250 and proposed #49252.
- @guanxingithub identified the shared-block ordering root cause in [scheduler traces](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49250#issuecomment-5430084907) and independently validated recovery.
- @he-yufeng contributed scheduler work in #45430 and #59793 and reviewed this PR.
- The linked [after-report reproducer](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-6167261048) and [before-report report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-6186695635) are from apex-mochen and ArijitDeb respectively.

</details>

### Follow-up: same-parent mechanism ablation

I ran a fresh 72-cell ablation: three modes, four source variants, baseline/reject, and three cold repetitions.

- **C**: exact PR base
- **S**: scheduler repair only
- **W**: minimal rewind marker plus worker device-offset rewind, without the scheduler repair
- **P**: exact PR head

| Mode | C | S | W | P |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sync OPT-125M | FAULT 3/3 | FAULT 3/3 | RECOVERED 3/3 | RECOVERED 3/3 |
| async OPT-125M | FAULT 3/3 | FAULT 3/3 | FAULT 3/3 | RECOVERED 3/3 |
| async EAGLE3 (2 drafts) | FAULT 3/3 | FAULT 3/3 | FAULT 3/3 | RECOVERED 3/3 |

`RECOVERED` means exact token-ID equality with the no-connector baseline. All baselines were stable. Every reject run promised one 16-token block, rejected it before copying KV, and exercised Model Runner V2; M3 also recorded nonzero EAGLE3 draft work.

This isolates the two parts of the fix:

- the worker device-offset rewind is necessary in all three modes;
- that rewind plus minimal marker plumbing is sufficient for sync; and
- the scheduler repair is additionally necessary for async and async EAGLE3.

An independent verifier re-read the raw results, logs, and connector events and reproduced all three classifications.

One control cell completed generation but needed a forced child-process kill during shutdown. Its functional evidence is intact, but this run does not establish clean resource shutdown. This is a new prospectively classified ablation and does not relabel the earlier M1 result.

Independent reproduction on this PR's own base, plus one observation that may be out of scope.

**Setup.** GH200, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (the example's default is a gated repo), 1 GPU, TP=1, `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`. Installed editable with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`, then swapped only the tracked `vllm/` tree between `d9fbe52` (base) and `819f20e` (head) so the PR is the only difference between arms. Verified per arm that `_mark_inflight_output_stale` is absent/present in the loaded source, rather than assuming the checkout took.

Running `examples/disaggregated/kv_load_failure_recovery_offline` step 3 (`decode_example.py --simulate-failure`):

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| `d9fbe52` (base) | `AssertionError` at `async_scheduler.py:63`, no output file |
| `819f20e` (head) | exit 0, recovery entered, **no assert**, output written |

So this PR does fix the crash, confirmed against a failing control on its own base.

**The observation.** On `819f20e` the run completes, but `sync_decode_recovered_output.txt` is not byte-identical to `decode_output.txt`, so `run.sh`'s `cmp` still fails:

```
-Generated text: '. I am a student, and I am learning'        # baseline
+Generated text: ". I'm a student who is studying Calculus"   # after recovery
```

Both examples use `temperature=0`, and 3 of the 4 prompts stay byte-identical — only the recovered request's text changes — so I don't think this is sampling noise.

That looks like #49250 rather than this PR: the title is "Restore state after KV load rejection" and you don't claim to fix the wrong-output half, so this may be entirely intended scope. Raising it only because `run.sh` ends in a `cmp`, so the example still doesn't pass end-to-end after this change, and a crash-only check would go green here.

**Caveat.** My arms differ only by `git checkout <sha> -- vllm/` on top of a single precompiled wheel, which is not the same as building each commit — if that invalidates the comparison, please say so. You've clearly done far more ablation on this path than I have, so I may be missing something obvious.

Happy to share full logs, the per-step `num_output_placeholders` traces, or re-run any variant you'd find useful. For what it's worth, the same example is what led me here: it doesn't appear to run in CI anywhere in the tree, which may be why three separate PRs have been open against this path.

@guanxingithub Thanks for the careful reproduction. I reproduced this with the
pinned Qwen3-0.6B revision and found two independent effects.

First, `819f20e` had a real shared-prefix recovery bug. One affected peer had
14 active in-flight tokens while the frame reporting the rejection contained
13, so the old code retained one optimistic token past the confirmed prefix.
Current head `ff85013` subtracts all active in-flight work without
double-counting already-stale output and adds shared-prefix/two-frame
regressions. The focused suite passes 60/60, and two cold Qwen rejection runs
now match connector-free recomputation for all four requests.

Second, successful external-KV reuse is not always token-identical to full
recomputation. In a separate control, external-KV reuse matched ordinary local
prefix-cache reuse for all four requests in both cold repetitions, while the
rejected path matched full recomputation. So the existing `run.sh` can still
fail even when recovery is correct: its final `cmp` uses successful external
reuse as the recovery oracle. The appropriate oracle here is connector-free
recomputation at the same decode configuration. I have documented that
distinction in the PR description; the example/connector cleanup is separate
follow-up work.

Your precompiled-wheel caveat does not invalidate this comparison: this PR's
delta is Python-only, and you verified the loaded source in each arm.

Verified `f2e2abd46` with the dual-oracle setup you suggested — it fixes both issues in my reproduction, and one correction to my earlier comment.

**Setup.** Same as before (GH200, Qwen3-0.6B, precompiled-wheel editable install, loaded source verified), plus two baselines at the same decode configuration: `oracleA` = decode with external KV present (successful reuse), `oracleB` = decode with `local_storage` removed so the connector finds nothing (full recomputation). One methodology note for anyone repeating this: the example connector is `kv_role="kv_both"`, so every decode run mutates `local_storage` — I restore a pristine snapshot before each arm.

**Result at `f2e2abd46`, default async scheduling:** recovery entered, no `num_output_placeholders` assert, exit 0, and per-prompt:

| prompt | rejected? | oracleA vs oracleB | recovered matches |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | yes | differ | **oracleB (full recompute)** |
| 2 | yes | identical | both |
| 3 | no | identical | both |
| 4 | no | differ | **oracleA (reuse)** |

Exactly the correct mix — rejected requests reproduce connector-free recomputation, unaffected requests keep reuse output. Also confirmed your oracle point by measurement: oracleA and oracleB legitimately differ at `temperature=0` (prompts 1 and 4), so any whole-file `cmp` on this path is the wrong check even for a correct fix.

**Correction to my earlier comment:** re-analyzing my `819f20e` run per-prompt against these oracles, that head already produced the same correct mix — my "recovered output differs from baseline" observation was this oracle artifact, not corruption. Sorry for the noise there; your one-optimistic-token find was real but did not show in my text comparison.

For completeness: the genuinely garbled recovery output I root-caused in vllm-project/vllm#49250 was measured on v0.27.1 (both scheduler modes), which predates this PR's serialization commit — I have not re-tested that tree and it is unaffected by this correction.

Thanks for the quick turnaround on both findings.

Thanks for the careful dual-oracle rerun and for correcting the earlier comparison. This is the intended per-request recovery behavior: rejected requests match connector-free full recomputation, while unaffected requests retain the successful-reuse path. The GH200 result at `f2e2abd46` is useful independent coverage.

For context, the serialization commit is also backed by a separate exact-`ff850131de` negative control: with `long_prefill_token_threshold=32`, the repair owner and dependent sharer were scheduled together before the shared repair frontier was restored. That control fails on `ff850131de` and passes on `f2e2abd46`. I've updated the PR description to keep that scheduler invariant separate from whole-file byte equality.

Thanks again for rerunning it and documenting the `kv_both` storage-reset detail.

A downstream data point for whoever picks this up for review.

NVIDIA's vLLM containers currently ship a config-level workaround for this path — we gate `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"` off entirely, because on the release we ship (v0.27.1-based) the recovery path either crashes the engine (async scheduling) or returns corrupted output (sync scheduling), and every crash-only mitigation we measured just converts the loud failure into a silent one. This PR is what lets us replace that gate with a real fix.

- The current head (`f2e2abd46`) is **independently verified** against the shipped reproduction: no `num_output_placeholders` assert, and recovered output per-request matches the correct oracle — rejected requests reproduce connector-free recomputation, unaffected requests keep external-reuse output ([details](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-5442764086)).

2. 3. The ownership/dependency machinery and the prefix-cache quarantine handle cross-request shared blocks, which #59793 never attempted.
4. The V2 runner rewind (sampled-state kernel restoring `total_len`/`last_sampled_token` and decrementing penalty bin counts, mamba state indices, thinking-budget caches) is the #49250 half done properly.

- `_rewind_sampled_state_kernel` decrements `output_bin_counts` for every token in the discarded suffix. That assumes every such token was counted when sampled. If a frame's tokens can be appended without passing through the penalties path (e.g. a replay or a warm-up path), the counts could go negative. Worth a second look; if appends always go through the counting path this is fine.
- In `_remove_request_from_kv_recovery`, when ownership transfers to a peer, the new owner's `required_end` is inherited from the departed owner. If the peer's own confirmed frontier is already past that end, the barrier releases on the next `_update_kv_recovery_progress` pass, so no deadlock, just one extra frame of conservatism. Fine as is.

I did not run the suite locally (no GPU box on my side); assessment is from code reading plus the shape of your test matrix, which covers the right cases (owner cancellation, deferred-peer transfer, quarantine of optimistic downstream blocks, fail-closed multi-group).

I found this case with a CPU-only scheduler fuzzer. It uses a fake external KV store with random sync/async load failures and checks that every position a scheduled request attends to holds that request's own token. On current `main` (`a2fb482732`), with `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, 3 of 60 seeds read KV from a block whose sync load failed and was never recomputed. All 3 had the same cause: the owner was aborted or preempted before recomputing, so the failed block was still in the prefix cache, and a later request (or the resumed owner) hit it. With this PR's head (`1eca68f4a2`), the same 60 seeds report nothing.

A deterministic test with the existing `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit` helpers. It fails on `main` and on this PR's base (`c077dc663d`) for `abort-recompute` and `preempt-recompute`, and passes all four cases on this PR's head. Feel free to take it if it is useful:

<details><summary>test_repro_recompute_pollution.py</summary>

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""Repro: with kv_load_failure_policy="recompute", a sync-load failure leaves the
failed blocks in the prefix cache. If the request that should recompute them goes
away first (aborted / preempted), a later request with the same prefix gets a
local prefix-cache hit on blocks whose KV was never loaded nor recomputed."""
from collections.abc import Callable

import pytest

from vllm.v1.request import Request, RequestStatus

from .utils import (
    create_mock_connector,
    create_model_runner_output,
    create_request,
    create_scheduler,
    create_vllm_config,
)

NUM_PROMPT_BLOCKS = 10
NUM_EXTERNAL_BLOCKS = 8
INVALID_BLOCK_IDX = 2


def _matched(table: dict[str, int]) -> Callable[[Request, int], tuple[int, bool]]:
    def f(request: Request, _: int) -> tuple[int, bool]:
        return table.get(request.request_id, 0), False

    return f


def _scheduler(policy: str):

    table = {a.request_id: NUM_EXTERNAL_BLOCKS * bs}
    sched.connector.get_num_new_matched_tokens.side_effect = _matched(table)

    out = sched.schedule()

    elif a.request_id in sched.requests:

## Overview

Fixes #49250 and addresses the stale-placeholder/request-stall mechanism in #45138. When a synchronous external KV load fails under `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, restore accepted request state in the scheduler and Model Runner V2 before decoding resumes.

## Claims

- Retire discarded in-flight output without changing the recovered request state.
- Restore V2 token history, sequence length, penalty counts, speculative state, and Mamba alignment state from the scheduler's accepted position.
- Order repair of shared KV blocks, prevent new prefix-cache hits on invalid blocks, and transfer unfinished repair ownership when an owner leaves after failure handling.

## Validation

At current head `1eca68f4`:

- [Author CPU validation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-6187605605): 497 selected cases passed. The after-report abort/preempt reproducer's two recompute cases fail on base; all four cases pass here.
- [Independent CPU validation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-6196459351): 74 recovery and invalid-block cases passed.
- [Targeted GPU validation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-6160858646): the suffix-rewind test passed, including non-negative penalty counts. Full-model GPU checks below belong to earlier revisions.

The upstream executor/connector CI lanes still require maintainer authorization, requested in the author validation comment above.

The historical local `22fdd4d9be` threshold-64 GPU dual-oracle result was **3/4**, with an unaffected request differing at a BF16 tie. This is not an all-output equality claim.

<details>
<summary>GPU history, reproduction and validation limits</summary>

Rejected requests are compared against connector-free recomputation; unaffected requests are compared against successful reuse. State and shared-block ordering are checked separately from exact token equality.

- [Independent GB200 run](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-6132316001), `c261cdee` applied to `main` `fabaecbf`: Qwen3-0.6B recovers where base asserts; the rejected prompt matches recomputation and the three unaffected prompts retain reuse output. 156 tests passed.
- [Independent GH200 run](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-5442764086), `f2e2abd460`: both rejected requests match recomputation and both unaffected requests match reuse.
- Local RTX 5060 Ti run, `22fdd4d9be` on base `eed1f3d0c6`: 330 tests passed and ten cold GPU cells completed. OPT-125M matched all eight baseline tokens after a rejected 16-token load with zero copied bytes. Qwen ordering passed at threshold 32 in sync/async modes and threshold 64 in sync mode. Threshold-64 exact dual-oracle equality was 3/4; threshold-32 whole-output differences also remained.
- Earlier controlled rejection covered sync, async, and async EAGLE3; real `LMCacheConnectorV1` negative controls covered sync and async. Failure was injected before KV copying. Direct old-versus-patched GPU controls also verified sampled-token/count rollback and Mamba offsets 0, 8, and 9.

The earlier local eight-file regression command was:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_kv_connector.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py
```

The 497-case CPU selection linked above is a separate run. Applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed in the earlier rebase validation. Updating this description did not rerun tests.

Not validated: real multi-GPU/NCCL execution, full-model Mamba/RecoverSSM load rejection, layerwise loading, partial-copy failure, performance, or cross-hardware bitwise determinism.

</details>

## Details

Scheduler rollback alone leaves device state from discarded frames. An explicit `rewound_req_ids` signal restores V2 state, while scheduler barriers prevent dependent requests from reading shared blocks before repair is safe. These parts address the same recovery sequence; there is no connector-specific special case.

<details>
<summary>Related work, remaining timing gaps and acknowledgements</summary>

#49252 derives a frame count from placeholders and excludes speculative decoding. This PR uses exact in-flight token accounting and an explicit worker rewind. #59793 covers the scheduler portion; [its author reviewed this PR and prefers it to land](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-6157413424), keeping #59793 as a fallback.

**Before-report gaps remain separate.** Aborting before the failure report can leave invalid blocks reusable, tracked in #61768 and addressed by #61769. Overlaying #61769 at `7238ccdf` onto `1eca68f4` passed 519 author CPU cases and 96 independent CPU cases. Those totals include the overlay and are not results for this PR alone. The [latest independent check](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-6196459351) also reports preemption before the failure report, which neither PR covers. If #61769 lands first, this PR will need a rebase retaining both sets of helper assertions.

When a rejected KV-load frame reaches the end of prefill and samples a token, `_post_update_kernel` has already incremented `total_len`, written `all_token_ids` and `last_sampled_tokens`, and updated `output_bin_counts`; overlapping async frames can add more such state. <details><summary>test_repro_recompute_pollution.py</summary>

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""Repro: with kv_load_failure_policy="recompute", a sync-load failure leaves the
failed blocks in the prefix cache. If the request that should recompute them goes
away first (aborted / preempted), a later request with the same prefix gets a
local prefix-cache hit on blocks whose KV was never loaded nor recomputed."""
from collections.abc import Callable

import pytest

from vllm.v1.request import Request, RequestStatus

from .utils import (
    create_mock_connector,
    create_model_runner_output,
    create_request,
    create_scheduler,
    create_vllm_config,
)

NUM_PROMPT_BLOCKS = 10
NUM_EXTERNAL_BLOCKS = 8
INVALID_BLOCK_IDX = 2


def _matched(table: dict[str, int]) -> Callable[[Request, int], tuple[int, bool]]:
    def f(request: Request, _: int) -> tuple[int, bool]:
        return table.get(request.request_id, 0), False

    return f


def _scheduler(policy: str):
    vllm_config = create_vllm_config()
    vllm_config.kv_transfer_config.kv_load_failure_policy = policy
    sched = create_scheduler(vllm_config)
    sched.connector = create_mock_connector()
    sched.connector.request_finished.return_value = (False, None)
    sched.connector.take_events.return_value = ()
    return sched


@pytest.mark.parametrize("policy", ["recompute", "fail"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("how", ["abort", "preempt"])
def test_failed_sync_blocks_not_reused_before_recompute(policy, how):
    sched = _scheduler(policy)
    bs = sched.block_size
    n = NUM_PROMPT_BLOCKS * bs
    a = create_request(request_id=1, num_tokens=n, common_prefix_len=n)
    table = {a.request_id: NUM_EXTERNAL_BLOCKS * bs}
    sched.connector.get_num_new_matched_tokens.side_effect = _matched(table)

    sched.add_request(a)
    out = sched.schedule()
    a_blocks = out.scheduled_new_reqs[0].block_ids[0]
    bad = a_blocks[INVALID_BLOCK_IDX]
    sched.update_from_output(
        out, create_model_runner_output([a], invalid_block_ids={bad}, use_eos=False)
    )

    # The external copy is gone (that is why the load failed), so from now on
    # only the local prefix cache can serve this prefix.
    table.clear()

    # A goes away before it gets to recompute the failed block.
    if how == "abort":
        sched.finish_requests([a.request_id], RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
    elif a.request_id in sched.requests:
        # As the scheduler does under KV pressure: pop from running, then preempt.
        sched.running.remove(a)
        sched._preempt_request(a, 0.0)

    # B: same prompt, no external hit -> only the local prefix cache can serve it.
    b = create_request(request_id=2, num_tokens=n, common_prefix_len=n)
    sched.add_request(b)
    out2 = sched.schedule()
    # Every request scheduled now attends to its tokens before this step's chunk;
    # none of those may sit in the failed, never-recomputed block.
    for req_id, n_sched in out2.num_scheduled_tokens.items():
        req = sched.requests[req_id]
        reused = req.num_computed_tokens - n_sched
        (blocks,) = sched.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(req_id)
        assert bad not in blocks[: reused // bs], (
            f"policy={policy} how={how}: {req_id} treats {reused} tokens as computed, "
            f"including block {bad} whose load failed and was never recomputed"
        )
```

If a request's sync KV load fails and the request is aborted in the same step, `_process_aborts_queue` frees it before `update_from_output` processes the failure report. `_handle_invalid_blocks` then finds no affected request in `running` or `kv_holding_waiting` and returns before evicting, so the never-loaded blocks stay prefix-cache hits. Here the repair owner is gone before any repair state could be registered, which is why the ownership transfer and quarantine in this PR can't see it; it also affects the default `fail` policy.
